scenario_stem:

Tidemere employs 2 part-time assistants and re-covers sofas, armchairs and dining chair seats for local households. Her friend Marcus Vale has offered to join as a 50% partner, contributing $40,000, or she could remain sole owner and hire an additional part-time assistant costing $12,000 a year. questions.question_text: Do you think Tallow Tree Bakery should franchise the new bakeries rather than keep them company-owned? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Franchising achieves the 18-month expansion without the company funding $300,000 of set-up costs (2 bakeries x $150,000) [k], because franchisees pay their own way while Tallow Tree collects $8,000 fees and 6% royalties [app], adding $16,000 of fee income plus a continuing royalty stream [an]. However, company-owned bakeries keep 100% of profits [k] and guarantee James complete control over quality, prices and brand standards [app], avoiding any franchisee disputes that could damage reputation [an]. Overall, Tallow Tree Bakery should franchise the two new bakeries [eval], because the 18-month target is met faster and cheaper while generating immediate fee income [eval].
